summary.text: 京 is interpreted as a picture of a tall building or platform; an old dictionary account instead describes a high man-made mound. Its common present meaning is “capital,” but how that sense arose is unresolved.

formation.text: Treat 京 as a whole pictograph of a tall built structure or platform. A competing account describes a high man-made mound; neither interpretation establishes a dated route to “capital.”

components.text: 京 is treated as one pictorial graph, not divided into modern-looking parts. Descriptions of early forms interpret them as a roof, tower, and wall; the selected oracle-style glyph is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact.

history.text: The selected oracle-bone-style redraw has a broad rooflike top, a central opening, and long lower strokes. It illustrates the building interpretation but is not a dated inscription.

Paleographic descriptions interpret oracle-bone and bronze forms as a tall building, and describe the small-seal form as simplifying its tower element to 口. The available account does not date or document the individual stages of this change.

uncertainties.text: 京 has competing interpretations as a tall building or platform and as a high man-made mound. A hilltop shrine or settlement has also been proposed to explain “capital,” but the route to that sense remains unresolved.
The earliest use of 京 for “capital” is undated. The evidence does not show whether the sense developed from a mound or settlement, followed another path, or represents a distinct word sense.

senses.text: 京 is interpreted as a tall building or platform; the Shuowen account instead describes a high man-made mound. The evidence does not resolve which interpretation best captures its earliest meaning.

senses.period: attested in a Tang poem by cited work; earliest use unresolved
senses.text: 京 means “capital city”; an example occurs in a cited Tang poem. This does not establish when the sense began or how it relates to the high-structure or mound interpretations.
“Large” is recorded as a sense, but its chronology and connection to the other meanings are not established.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a chronological semantic link between the high-structure or mound interpretations and “capital” or “large.”
